description: Establish the Python backtester package skeleton, the reproducible data-extract helper, and the streaming tick data loader + M5 bar aggregator. This is the foundation the engine and strategy build on. First establish the in-sandbox baseline (existing tools=16 and tuner=38 test suites green) so we know we started from green. Then add python_bt/ package, data/extract.py (regenerates the gitignored 526MB CSV from the tracked split chunks using stdlib zipfile only), a streaming loader that yields tick events without loading the whole file into memory, and a ticks->M5 bar aggregator. Include stdlib unittest tests using tiny inline fixtures (never the 526MB file). STDLIB ONLY, pure ASCII, target Python 3.9+.
steps: BASELINE: run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' -q` (expect 16 OK) and `cd automation/tuner && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q` (expect 38 OK). Confirm both green BEFORE writing new code so the baseline is known-good. Note python3 is 3.9.25 (python3.11/3.12 also present); write code compatible with 3.9 (no match/case; use `from __future__ import annotations` if using PEP 604 unions).

PACKAGE SKELETON: create python_bt/ as a package with __init__.py, and python_bt/tests/__init__.py. Plan modules (created here and in later features): python_bt/loader.py (this feature), python_bt/bars.py (this feature), python_bt/engine.py + python_bt/broker.py + python_bt/metrics.py (FEAT-002), python_bt/strategy/__init__.py + base.py + gagan.py (FEAT-003), python_bt/runner.py + python_bt/research.py (FEAT-003/004). Add a python_bt/config.py holding the flagged instrument constants: POINT_SIZE=0.01 (detected from XAUUSD 2-decimal quotes; comment: CONFIRM vs broker), CONTRACT_SIZE=100 (oz; $1.00 move = $100 per 1.0 lot; CONFIRM), TICK_SIZE=0.01, TICK_VALUE=1.0 (USD per TICK_SIZE per 1.0 lot; CONFIRM), COMMISSION_PER_LOT_PER_SIDE (Fusion commission; e.g. 3.5 USD/lot/side as a documented default; CONFIRM), INITIAL_DEPOSIT=1000.0, LEVERAGE=500. Every constant gets an ASCII comment flagging it as a parity assumption the user must confirm.

EXTRACT HELPER data/extract.py: a stdlib-only (zipfile, os, sys, argparse, hashlib optional) script that regenerates the CSV from the tracked chunks. Logic: (1) if the final CSV data/XAUUSD_202607011100_202609011203/XAUUSD_202607011100_202609011203.csv already exists and is non-empty, print and exit 0 (idempotent) unless --force. (2) Otherwise concatenate data/XAUUSD_202607011100_202609011203_2.zip.001 .. .005 in numeric order into data/joined.bin by streaming in binary chunks (shutil.copyfileobj or fixed-size reads; do NOT read all into memory). (3) Open data/joined.bin with zipfile.ZipFile -> it contains the INNER archive XAUUSD_202607011100_202609011203.zip -> extract that inner zip to data/ -> open the inner zip -> extract the CSV into data/XAUUSD_202607011100_202609011203/. (4) Print the final CSV path, its size, and the first data line for confirmation. Handle both the 2-level nesting (outer joined -> inner zip -> csv) verified in-repo. Provide a callable function extract_csv(data_dir='data', force=False) -> csv_path AND an argparse CLI (`python3 data/extract.py [--force]`). Keep it robust: clear error if a chunk is missing. Do NOT commit joined.bin or the CSV (already gitignored).

STREAMING LOADER python_bt/loader.py: define a Tick as a lightweight structure (dataclass or a plain tuple factory) carrying ts (datetime with millisecond precision), bid (float), ask (float). Write iter_ticks(csv_path, date_from=None, date_to=None) as a GENERATOR that opens the file with open(csv_path, 'r', newline='') and iterates line by line (NEVER read()/readlines() the whole file). Parse the tab-separated columns; skip the header row (starts with '<DATE>'); parse DATE 'YYYY.MM.DD' + TIME 'HH:MM:SS.mmm' into a datetime (handle the optional missing milliseconds and the CRLF line endings); tolerate empty LAST/VOLUME/FLAGS; skip malformed/blank lines without crashing. date_from/date_to (datetime or 'YYYY.MM.DD' string) slice the stream: skip ticks before date_from, stop iteration once past date_to (early-return for speed). Provide an optional max_ticks arg for quick smoke runs. Keep the hot loop tight: use str.split('\t'), avoid csv module overhead if measurably slower, avoid per-tick object churn where reasonable. Add a small helper parse_ts(date_str, time_str) -> datetime that tests can call directly.

M5 BAR AGGREGATOR python_bt/bars.py: define a Bar structure (ts_open datetime aligned to bar boundary, open, high, low, close, tick_count; use the MID or a chosen price - document choosing mid=(bid+ask)/2 for OHLC and carry the last bid/ask so the engine can still fill at spread). Write iter_bars(tick_iterable, timeframe_minutes=5) as a GENERATOR that consumes the tick stream and yields a completed Bar each time the M5 boundary rolls over (bucket by flooring ts to timeframe_minutes). OHLC built from the mid price of each tick within the bucket; also expose last bid/ask of the bar so strategies running on bar closes still fill at realistic spread. Emit the final partial bar at end of stream. This gives both a tick feed (loader) and a bar feed (bars) so strategies can run on M5 bars reconstructed from real ticks while fills stay tick/quote aware. Boundary alignment must be deterministic (floor minute to multiple of timeframe_minutes, seconds/micros zeroed).

TESTS python_bt/tests/test_loader.py + test_bars.py: use tiny INLINE fixtures (write a few-line temp CSV in the exact verified tab format incl. the '<DATE>' header, CRLF, empty LAST/VOLUME, ms timestamps, and a malformed line). Assert: header skipped; ts parsed with millisecond precision; bid/ask floats correct; empty LAST/VOLUME tolerated; malformed line skipped not crashed; date_from/date_to slicing includes/excludes correctly and stops early; max_ticks respected. For bars: feed a hand-built tick list spanning >2 M5 buckets and assert bar count, OHLC (open=first mid, high=max mid, low=min mid, close=last mid), boundary alignment, and that the final partial bar is emitted. Do NOT read the 526MB CSV in tests.

VERIFY: python3 -m py_compile python_bt/*.py python_bt/tests/*.py data/extract.py; python3 -m unittest discover -s python_bt/tests -p 'test_*.py' -q (all green); run `python3 data/extract.py` and confirm it (re)produces the CSV from just the chunks and prints size ~526MB + 11,861,292-ish rows worth (report the printed first line); grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]' on all new files (empty); re-run tools (16) and tuner (38) suites (still green); git status confirms GaganEA.mq5 untouched and no big data files staged.
acceptance_criteria: python3 -m py_compile succeeds on every new .py file (python_bt/*.py, python_bt/tests/*.py, data/extract.py).

`python3 data/extract.py` regenerates data/XAUUSD_202607011100_202609011203/XAUUSD_202607011100_202609011203.csv from ONLY the tracked split chunks using stdlib zipfile, and is idempotent (a second run does not re-extract unless --force).

iter_ticks streams the file line-by-line (no full-file read) and correctly parses the verified tab format: header skipped, ms-precision datetime, float bid/ask, empty LAST/VOLUME tolerated, malformed lines skipped, date_from/date_to slice with early stop, max_ticks honored.
iter_bars aggregates ticks into aligned M5 bars with correct OHLC from mid price, exposes last bid/ask, and emits the final partial bar.
New python_bt unittest suite passes with tiny inline fixtures and does NOT depend on the 526MB CSV.
All new files are pure ASCII (grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]' empty). GaganEA.mq5 is untouched. No big data files staged for commit.
Existing suites still green: tools 16 tests, tuner 38 tests.
verification: python3 -m py_compile python_bt/loader.py python_bt/bars.py python_bt/config.py data/extract.py
python3 data/extract.py  (prints regenerated CSV path + size + first data line)
cd automation/tuner && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q  (expect 38 OK)
